subtitle: Unofficial Chautauqua guide
promotionalText: New in 1.1.3: a day rail above the events list — tap any day to jump straight to it, or ask Siri to show you tomorrow.
disclaimer: CHQ Calendar is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution. Event information is drawn from publicly posted listings; chq.org remains the authoritative source.
description:
CHQ Calendar is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution. Event information is drawn from publicly posted listings; chq.org remains the authoritative source.

Planning a day on the grounds shouldn't take longer than the day itself.

CHQ Calendar puts the whole Chautauqua season in one place, then helps you act on it — reminders for what you've starred, a plan for your day, and a map to get there.

NEVER MISS WHAT YOU STARRED
• Star an event to get a reminder — 30 minutes before, 1 hour before, or the night before
• Set a default reminder timing once, or override it per event
• Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets show what's next on the grounds, or just your starred events
• Widgets are configurable by venue, category, or starred-only

PLAN YOUR DAY
• My Day lays your starred events out on a timeline
• Flags schedule overlaps and tight walking gaps between venues
• Updates automatically as you star or unstar events

FIND YOUR WAY
• Every venue on the grounds plotted on a map
• Tap a venue for its next events and walking directions
• Jump to the map from any event's detail screen
• No location permission required

BROWSE THE SEASON
• Every event of the season, grouped by day
• Filter by category, venue, and week; search by name, venue, or presenter
• Full event details, including linked Chautauquan Daily articles
• Save favorites so you don't lose track of what you can't miss

WORKS EVERYWHERE
• Events you've already loaded stay readable offline
• Built for both iPhone and iPad
• Ask Siri — say “Chautauqua” and ask what’s next, what’s on tonight, who’s speaking, or this week’s theme
• Find events instantly from system-wide Spotlight search
• Quick links to Chautauqua’s own services, including live captioning for attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing
• Off-season, see a countdown to next season, browse announced events, and revisit past seasons

No account. No ads. No third-party trackers. Your filters, favorites, and reminders stay on your device.

Event information comes from publicly posted Chautauqua Institution listings and from local organizations that publish their own events. For ticketing, official announcements, and the last word on any event, visit chq.org.
whatsNew:
Version 1.1.3 is about moving through the season.

A DAY AT A TIME
• A day rail sits above the events list — tap any day to jump straight to it
• Step a day at a time with the chevrons, or tap ⟳ Now to come back to today
• The list grows as you reach its edges instead of stopping at the end
• Each day names how many events it holds, so an empty day is visible before you tap it

ASK FOR A DAY
• “Show me tomorrow in Chautauqua” now opens the app on tomorrow
• Siri and the day rail land in exactly the same place

ACCESSIBILITY
• The Filters button no longer clips its label at the largest text sizes
reviewNotes:
CHQ Calendar is an unofficial, independent app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Chautauqua Institution, and it says so in three places: the first paragraph of the App Store description, the app's About screen (toolbar > info button), and the website at https://www.chqcal.org/privacy.

The app displays publicly posted event information for the Chautauqua Institution summer season — dates, times, titles, venues, presenters. Every event links back to chq.org, which the app identifies as the authoritative source.

Data is served from https://www.chqcal.org, a website operated by the developer.

No account or login is required. There is no gated content and no demo credentials are needed — launching the app shows the full feature set immediately.

The app itself contains no analytics or tracking SDKs and no advertising identifiers, and it has no accounts — preferences and cached event data remain on device, and calendar access is write-only, used only for events the user explicitly chooses to add. The website that serves the app's data, https://www.chqcal.org, keeps standard CDN access logs and derives a pseudonymous key from IP address and user-agent to count unique and returning visitors in aggregate. This is declared in App Privacy as Usage Data (Product Interaction): not linked to identity, not used for tracking, and never shared with third parties.

iOS-specific capabilities, introduced in 1.1 as the response to the prior 4.2 review and extended since: every item below is reachable within seconds of launch, no configuration required to see it exists.
- Reminders — star any event (list or detail view), then use the "Remind me" row in the event detail screen to pick 30 minutes before, 1 hour before, or the night before at 8 PM. A default preset is set in the app's About screen (toolbar > info button) > Reminders.
- Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets — add "Next Up" (Home Screen small/medium, Lock Screen rectangular/inline; configurable by venue, category, or starred-only) or "Starred" (Home Screen small, Lock Screen rectangular) from the iOS widget gallery under CHQ Calendar. Off-season, both show a countdown to next season instead of an empty widget.
- My Day tab — the starred events a user has chosen, laid out on a timeline, flagging schedule overlaps and tight walking gaps between venues.
- Map tab — every venue on the grounds plotted, with a tap-through sheet showing that venue's next events, a filter to show only that venue's events in the list, and walking directions that open in Apple Maps. The app requests no location permission for any of this.
- Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight — seven Shortcuts actions, listed in the Shortcuts app under CHQ Calendar as "What's Next", "Today", "Open Event", "Weekly Theme", "My Schedule", "Who's Speaking", and "Show Time", each of which also runs by voice through Siri. The app registers "Chautauqua", "Chautauqua Calendar", and "CHQ" as alternative app names, so a phrase such as "What's happening tonight in Chautauqua?" routes to the app; the About screen (toolbar > info button) lists example phrases and links straight to the Shortcuts app. System-wide Spotlight search indexes the season's events plus every starred event, and a tapped result opens directly to that event.
- Off-season experience — outside the summer season the app opens to a countdown to next season, a preview of next season's announced events (once chq.org has published them), and browsable access to past seasons, instead of an empty screen.

New in 1.1.2, relative to the 1.1 build previously reviewed:
- The Siri vocabulary above grew from three actions to seven, and the app now registers alternative spoken names so a user can say "Chautauqua" rather than the full app name.
- The toolbar's More menu gained a link to Chautauqua Institution's live captioning service at https://captions.chq.org, for attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing. It opens in the user's browser; the app neither hosts nor proxies that service, and Chautauqua Institution operates it.
- My Day now opens on the current day and can be moved through the season a day at a time.
- Corrections to date filtering, and a performance fix to starring an event. No new permissions and no new data collection.

All of the above uses local notifications only — no push notifications, no server-side scheduling, no location permission, and no new data collection beyond what is already declared above.
